chapters.title: Chapter 2: Before You File: Documents and Pre-Checks

lessons.title: PAN, Aadhaar and Your Income Tax Portal Account: Getting Set Up

body.text: Most filing disasters happen before you open a single ITR form. An inoperative PAN, a bank account that was never validated, or a mobile number that no longer works can block your return or your refund, no matter how accurate your numbers are.

children.text: This lesson is the setup work. Three things need to be in order before July: your PAN, its link with Aadhaar, and your account on the e-filing portal, including a bank account the department can actually pay your refund into. Do this in May or June, not on 30 July at midnight.

markDefs.definition: Permanent Account Number. A 10-character alphanumeric identifier issued by the Income Tax Department. Every return, TDS credit, tax payment and refund is tracked against it.

children.text: is governed by Section 262 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Section 139A of the Income-tax Act, 1961). It must be quoted in your return, in every tax payment challan and in all correspondence with the department. Your employer quotes it when depositing TDS on your salary, your bank quotes it for TDS on your FD, and Zerodha or Groww report your trades against it. It is the thread that ties all of your tax data together.

cells: 1 to 3
AFK
An alphabetic series running from AAA to ZZZ
P
Type of holder. P means individual (person)
S
For individuals, the first letter of the surname, here Sharma
6 to 9
A sequential number from 0001 to 9999
M
An alphabetic check character

body.title: Read the Fourth Character
body.question: Your uncle runs the family's investments through a PAN whose fourth character is H. What kind of taxpayer does this PAN belong to?
body.explanation: H stands for Hindu Undivided Family. P is an individual, C a company, F a firm (including an LLP), T a trust and A an association of persons. An HUF is a separate taxpayer from the uncle himself, with its own PAN and its own ITR.

body.text: One person, one PAN. Holding two PANs, often the result of applying again after losing a card, can attract a penalty of ₹10,000. If you have a duplicate, surrender it through the PAN change or correction request with NSDL (Protean) or UTIITSL. If you have lost your card, download a free e-PAN instead of applying for a new number.

children.text: The PAN-Aadhaar Link: Operative or Inoperative

markDefs.definition: A PAN that has not been linked with Aadhaar by the required date. It still exists, but cannot be used normally: refunds are withheld and TDS and TCS apply at higher rates until it is made operative again.

children.text: Every individual who holds a PAN and is eligible for Aadhaar must intimate their Aadhaar number to the department, under Section 262 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Section 139AA of the Income-tax Act, 1961). If you do not, your PAN becomes

. The general deadline passed on 30 June 2023. A second group, people who were allotted a PAN on the basis of an Aadhaar enrolment ID rather than the actual Aadhaar number, had to complete the link by 31 December 2025.

body.title: How the PAN-Aadhaar Deadline Played Out

events.title: Linking Made Mandatory
events.description: Section 139AA required individuals eligible for Aadhaar to quote it and link it with their PAN.

events.title: Free Linking Ends
events.description: After several extensions, the window to link without any fee closed.

events.title: Fee Rises to ₹1,000
events.description: After a short period at ₹500, the fee for late linking settled at ₹1,000.

events.title: Unlinked PANs Become Inoperative
events.description: PANs not linked by 30 June 2023 became inoperative, with refunds withheld and higher TDS and TCS rates.

events.title: Deadline for PANs Issued on Enrolment ID
events.description: People allotted a PAN using an Aadhaar enrolment ID had to link their actual Aadhaar number by this date.

events.title: Second Wave of Inoperative PANs
events.description: Those who missed the 31 December 2025 deadline saw their PANs become inoperative.

body.title: What Changes When Your PAN Goes Inoperative

columns.label: Operative PAN
points: Refunds processed and credited to your pre-validated bank account
Interest paid on refunds as per the law
TDS on FD interest at 10% above the threshold
Normal TCS rates on foreign remittances and tour packages
Smooth return filing, KYC and investment transactions

columns.label: Inoperative PAN
points: Refunds not issued while the PAN stays inoperative
No interest on the refund for the period the PAN was inoperative
TDS generally at 20%, or twice the normal rate if higher
Problems with filing, bank and demat KYC, and mutual fund transactions

body.title: The Cost of an Inoperative PAN
body.prompt: Manoj, 45, a shop owner in Nagpur, earns ₹80,000 of FD interest from Bank of Baroda in FY 2025-26. His PAN is inoperative because he never linked Aadhaar. Normally TDS would be 10%. How much extra TDS does the bank deduct because his PAN is inoperative?
body.explanation: With an operative PAN, TDS would be 10% of ₹80,000, or ₹8,000. With an inoperative PAN it is 20%, the higher of 20% and twice the normal rate, so ₹16,000. The extra ₹8,000 is not lost forever, but it is stuck: the refund will not be issued while the PAN stays inoperative, and no interest accrues on it for that period.

children.text: Who Does Not Need to Link

The linking requirement does not apply to individuals residing in Assam, Jammu and Kashmir or Meghalaya, to non-residents as defined in the Act, to people aged 80 or more at any time during the year, and to those who are not citizens of India. Note that an NRI whose residential status is not updated in the PAN database may still show as inoperative, so update your status if you fall in that group.

body.title: Check and Fix Your PAN-Aadhaar Link
steps: On incometax.gov.in, go to Quick Links and select Link Aadhaar Status. Enter your PAN and Aadhaar number
If it shows linked, you are done. Take a screenshot for your records
If not linked, pay the ₹1,000 fee through e-Pay Tax, selecting Major Head 0021 and Minor Head 500
Wait 4 to 5 working days for the payment to reflect
Log in, go to Link Aadhaar on the dashboard, and submit the request with an OTP sent to your Aadhaar-registered mobile
Check your status again after some days. The PAN typically becomes operative within 30 days of the request
If your name, date of birth or gender do not match between PAN and Aadhaar, correct the mismatch first, or the link will fail

body.label: Late Linking Fee
body.context: Levied under Section 234H of the Income-tax Act, 1961 and payable before submitting the link request. Start by early June if you want your PAN operative before the July filing deadline.

body.title: Refund Stuck in Indore
body.scenario: Rakesh, 34, a sales manager in Indore, never linked his PAN with Aadhaar, assuming it was optional. For FY 2025-26, TDS on his FD interest was deducted at 20% instead of 10%, and he expects a refund of about ₹12,000. It is now 5 July 2026 and he wants to file before 31 July.
body.prompt: What problems is Rakesh facing, and what should he do, in what order?
body.modelAnswer: His PAN is inoperative, which explains the 20% TDS. While it remains inoperative, any refund will not be issued and he will not earn interest on it for that period, and he may have trouble filing at all. His steps: first, check Link Aadhaar Status on the portal to confirm. Second, make sure his name, date of birth and gender match exactly across PAN and Aadhaar, correcting any mismatch. Third, pay the ₹1,000 late fee through e-Pay Tax under Major Head 0021, Minor Head 500. Fourth, wait 4 to 5 working days, then submit the Link Aadhaar request with the Aadhaar OTP. The PAN can take up to about 30 days to become operative, so it may not be ready by 31 July. He should file as early as the portal allows, still aiming for the due date, since a late return costs him a late fee and on-time benefits. Once the PAN is operative, his refund will be processed. Next year he should also expect normal 10% TDS on his FD interest.

children.text: Everything in this course happens on one site: incometax.gov.in. Your login ID is your PAN. Registration takes about ten minutes if you have your PAN, a working mobile number and an email ID you actually check.

cells: On the home page, click Register and choose Taxpayer
Only use incometax.gov.in. Ignore links in SMS or WhatsApp messages
Enter your PAN and click Validate
If the portal says the PAN is already registered, use Forgot Password instead
Enter name, date of birth, gender and residential status exactly as per PAN
A mismatch here is the most common reason registration fails
Enter your primary mobile number, email ID and address
Use your own mobile and email, not your CA's or a family member's
Enter the 6-digit OTPs sent to your mobile and email
Non-residents receive the OTP on email
Set a password and a personalised secure access message, then click Register
Use a strong password with upper and lower case letters, a number and a special character

body.text: The secure access message you set during registration appears every time you log in, before you enter your password. If you ever land on a login page that does not show your message, you are on a fake site. Phishing emails promising an income tax refund are one of the most common scams during filing season, and the real department never asks for your card details or OTP by email or SMS.

body.title: Other ways to log in, and what to do if you forget your password

children.text: Apart from PAN and password, you can log in through net banking: most major banks, including SBI, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank, offer an e-filing login option that redirects you to the portal without a password. You can also use an OTP on your Aadhaar-registered mobile, provided your PAN and Aadhaar are linked. If you forget your password, use Forgot Password on the login page and reset it with an Aadhaar OTP, a net banking login, or an OTP on your registered mobile and email.
Three Profile Settings to Fix Before Filing

markDefs.definition: A bank account whose details the portal has checked with your bank against your PAN and name. Refunds are credited only to a pre-validated account.

children.text: First, your bank account. Go to My Profile, then My Bank Account, then Add Bank Account. Enter the account number, type and IFSC, and click Validate. Refunds are credited only to a

, and validation succeeds only if the account is linked with your PAN and your name matches the bank's records. Second, enable EVC on one pre-validated account so you can e-verify your return through it. EVC can be active on only one account at a time. Third, check your contact details under My Profile. Every OTP and every intimation about your return goes to that mobile and email.

stats.label: OTP Length
stats.context: Sent to mobile and email during registration

body.title: Where Does the Refund Go?
body.textWithBlank: The Income Tax Department credits refunds only to a ___ bank account linked to your PAN.
body.explanation: Refunds go only to a bank account that has been pre-validated on the e-filing portal. An old account you closed years ago, or one that is not linked to your PAN, will cause the refund to fail.

body.label: Check Your PAN-Aadhaar Link Status
body.description: Open the e-filing portal home page and use Quick Links, then Link Aadhaar Status. No login needed.

body.title: Your Setup Checklist for Filing Season
steps: Confirm you hold exactly one PAN, and download your e-PAN if the physical card is lost
Check that your PAN and Aadhaar are linked, or that you fall in an exempt category
Register on incometax.gov.in, or confirm your existing login still works
Set or note your secure access message
Update your mobile number and email ID under My Profile
Add and pre-validate the bank account where you want your refund
Enable EVC on that pre-validated account

points: Your PAN, under Section 262 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Section 139A of the 1961 Act), is the identifier every TDS credit, return and refund is tracked against, and you may hold only one

PAN must be linked with Aadhaar under Section 262 (Section 139AA of the 1961 Act); unlinked PANs became inoperative from 1 July 2023, and PANs issued on an Aadhaar enrolment ID had to be linked by 31 December 2025
An inoperative PAN means refunds withheld, no refund interest for that period, and TDS and TCS at higher rates, often 20%
To restore it, pay the ₹1,000 fee under Major Head 0021 and Minor Head 500, wait 4 to 5 working days, then submit the link request
Register on incometax.gov.in with your PAN, own mobile and email, and set a secure access message to spot fake sites
Pre-validate your bank account and enable EVC on it before filing, since refunds only go to pre-validated accounts
